subject: Keepalive: short trial extension vs credit top-up — pricing ask
messages:
From: Brittany Cole <brittany@catalyzehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@catalyzehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Trial runway — short extension or credit?

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

We wrapped up internal demos this week and the analytics team needs just a bit more runway to validate latency at scale. Our current 30-day time-boxed eval has two weeks left. Before we escalate to procurement, I wanted to check options:

- Can Redwood add a short 2-week extension to the existing pilot at no extra charge?
- Alternatively, can we top up tokens/credits for the remainder of the pilot (so we keep the end date) and apply a small one-time discount to the top-up?

Procurement asked for a quick read on what each path would mean for billing and conversion — if we go with a credit top-up, will that be invoiced immediately? If we extend the term, is there any SLA or billing change?

Attached is a short note from our engineering lead summarizing the test they want to run.

Thanks,
Brittany
Brittany Cole
Director, Product Analytics
Catalyze Health

Attachment: catalyze-test-plan.txt (referenced)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Brittany Cole <brittany@catalyzehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial runway — short extension or credit?

Hi Brittany — thanks for the clear ask and the engineering note. Two feasible options from our side:

Option A — Short extension (2 weeks):
- We can extend the existing time-boxed pilot by 14 days.
- No additional invoice up front; we treat this as a one-time grace extension tied to the current POC.
- If you convert to a paid plan within 30 days of the extension end, we can commit to preserving the pilot pricing tier for the first month of production.

Option B — Credit top-up (keeps end date):
- We can add a one-time credit allocation to your existing pilot (covers X tokens / Y concurrent throughput).
- This would be invoiced as a one-off line item; we can apply a 10% promotional discount on the top-up for this trial.
- Credits are non-refundable but transferable to the initial production contract if you sign within 60 days.

Quick notes: both options preserve audit logs/audit access and trial observability in Redwood Console. Extension (A) helps time-based experiments where the test needs steady-state behavior; top-up (B) is better if you need burst capacity now.

I attached a short spreadsheet with estimated token coverage per option and ballpark pricing so you can share with procurement — see "Catalyze_Proposal_Options.xlsx".

If you prefer, we can also do a hybrid: 1-week free extension + smaller top-up at 5% discount. Which does procurement prefer?

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Catalyze_Proposal_Options.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Brittany Cole <brittany@catalyzehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial runway — short extension or credit?

Hi Brittany — looping in Sean from pricing/legal for a quick confirmation on standard terms.

Internal guidance from pricing: we can do either Option A or B. A couple of clarifications for procurement:

- If you take Option A (extension), we will not change the PO/ billing schedule; the pilot remains as-is and the extension is added as an amendment to the existing evaluation order. No separate invoice unless you request an expedited engineering uplift.
- If you take Option B (credit top-up), we will generate a single invoice for the credit top-up (net 30 by default). We can push an invoice reduction (10% promo) as Kimberly suggested; this requires a short approval and an internal discount code.

Legal/pricing note: we cannot extend the pilot more than 30 days without a signed SOW that includes conversion terms. I've attached a light SOW draft (Catalyze_SOW_Draft.pdf) that we can fill in if you need longer runway.

If procurement wants the fastest route, Option B (credit top-up + 10% promo) gets you immediate capacity with a clean invoice path. If you want the simplest contractual flow with no invoice, we do the 2-week extension under Option A.

Happy to jump on a 15-min call with procurement to finalize.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Catalyze_SOW_Draft.pdf

From: Brittany Cole <brittany@catalyzehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial runway — short extension or credit?

Hi Marissa / Kimberly,

Thanks — procurement reviewed both routes. Given timing constraints for our analytics cadence, we prefer Option B: a credit top-up with the 10% promotional discount. Procurement asked for:

1) A one-line invoice they can pay via our standard PO process (net 30).
2) A DocuSign link for a short amendment that states the top-up amount, discount applied, and credit-transfer-to-production clause.

If you can send the invoice + DocuSign by tomorrow morning, we can process same week and schedule the final load test for Monday.

Appreciate the quick turn — Brittany

--
Brittany Cole
Director, Product Analytics
Catalyze Health
